feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
Committing to a masked script in the absence of conditionals provides the same capabilities as codeseparator. Without commitment to the masked script, and lacking both conditionals and codeseparator, it becomes challenging for a signature to indicate which alternative script is being signed. However, this limitation can be addressed by assigning each alternative script within the MAST (Merkelized Abstract Syntax Tree) a slightly different key, which effectively differentiates them.
A comparison between traditional scripting approaches using IF statements and CODESEP and their taproot-based equivalents reveals notable differences in efficiency. For example, utilizing code such as DEPTH 3 EQUAL IF <Bob> CHECKSIGVERIFY HASH160 <H> EQUALVERIFY CODESEP ELSE <n> CLTV DROP ENDIF <Alice> CHECKSIG demonstrates that the IF+CODESEP approach can be more cost-effective, particularly when the S1 branch is executed most of the time. This efficiency arises because the overhead associated with "DEPTH 3 EQUAL IF/ELSE/ENDIF CODESEP <n> CLTV DROP" is lower than the 32-byte overhead required for selecting a Merkle branch in taproot constructions.
Nevertheless, questions remain regarding the necessity of Alice’s signature within the S1 branch; excluding it could make the taproot approach consistently cheaper. Furthermore, scriptless scripts offer even greater savings in terms of efficiency and cost.
Since these features primarily influence the behavior of signature verification operators, any disabled feature such as codeseparator could be reinstated relatively easily in future upgrades, such as during a transition from one witness version to another.
